topics.title: Linear Programming
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Form linear inequalities based on real life situations. (u, s)
Represent the inequalities on the graph and identifies the required region. (u, s)
Find and interpret the optimum solution of a set of linear inequalities in two unknowns. (u, s, v/a)

body.text: Linear programming turns a real-world limits problem into a set of linear inequalities, graphs the region that satisfies all of them (the feasible region), then finds the best (optimum) point within that region. A farmer has 32 acres for corn (x acres) and soybean (y acres): x >= 0, y >= 0, x+y <= 32 are the basic constraints, plus any cost or storage limits given.

Each constraint is graphed as a boundary line, with the unwanted side shaded out, leaving the feasible region where every inequality holds at once. The optimum solution (maximum profit or minimum cost) always occurs at a corner (vertex) of the feasible region — so instead of testing every point inside, only the corners need to be checked.

A mother buys x notebooks at UGX 600 each and y pens at UGX 800 each, with at least 4 notebooks and 4 pens, and at most UGX 8000 to spend. The constraints are: x>=4, y>=4, 600x+800y<=8000. Testing the corners of the resulting feasible region for the combination that uses the budget most fully identifies the optimum purchase.
